root.name: Benko Gambit Accepted: Pawn Return Variation

overview: White plays 5.b6, returning the pawn to avoid the Benko compensation. After 5...Qxb6 (or 5...d6, 5...e6) Black has regained the pawn and gets an easy game with the queen out early; White usually develops with Nc3 and e4 and takes the d5/e4 centre. The position becomes a Benoni-like structure.

white_ideas.idea: Return the pawn with b6 to avoid the long-term Benko pressure
Play Nc3 and e4 to take the centre
Develop with Bd3 and Nge2 or Nf3 and keep a space edge

black_ideas.idea: Recapture with ...Qxb6 and develop with ...g6 and ...Bg7
Play ...d6 and ...e6 for a Benoni-style set-up
Challenge the d5 pawn with ...e6 or ...Nbd7

typical_structures.structure: Benoni-like structure with White d5/e4 against Black c5/d6
Black queen on b6 early with a fianchetto bishop

character.notes: The pawn comes back at once, leaving a quiet Benoni-like position with small edges.

gambit.notes: White returns the pawn with b6 and Black wins it back by force with ...Qxb6.

soundness.notes: Sound; just an easy equal game for Black.

structure.notes: Asymmetric centre, d5 against c5/d6: semi-open.

approach.notes: A known way for White to avoid the Benko; standard.

level.notes: Typical Benoni-like plans, not much to memorise.

character.reason: Pawn comes back and a quiet middlegame follows.

gambit.reason: White returns the pawn immediately; no material is lost by force.

approach.reason: A known branch of the Benko.

plans.reason: Black fianchettoes while White holds the space with d5 and e4.
